title: A. Harry Potter and Three Spells

legend: A long time ago (probably even in the first book), Nicholas Flamel, a great alchemist and the creator of the Philosopher's Stone, taught Harry Potter three useful spells. The first one allows you to convert a grams of sand into b grams of lead, the second one allows you to convert c grams of lead into d grams of gold and third one allows you to convert e grams of gold into f grams of sand. When Harry told his friends about these spells, Ron Weasley was amazed. After all, if they succeed in turning sand into lead, lead into gold, and then turning part of the gold into sand again and so on, then it will be possible to start with a small amount of sand and get huge amounts of gold! Even an infinite amount of gold! Hermione Granger, by contrast, was skeptical about that idea. She argues that according to the law of conservation of matter getting an infinite amount of matter, even using magic, is impossible. On the contrary, the amount of matter may even decrease during transformation, being converted to magical energy. Though Hermione's theory seems convincing, Ron won't believe her. As far as Ron is concerned, Hermione made up her law of conservation of matter to stop Harry and Ron wasting their time with this nonsense, and to make them go and do homework instead. That's why Ron has already collected a certain amount of sand for the experiments. A quarrel between the friends seems unavoidable...

Help Harry to determine which one of his friends is right, and avoid the quarrel after all. To do this you have to figure out whether it is possible to get the amount of gold greater than any preassigned number from some finite amount of sand.
input: The first line contains 6 integers a, b, c, d, e, f (0 ≤ a, b, c, d, e, f ≤ 1000).
output: Print "Ron", if it is possible to get an infinitely large amount of gold having a certain finite amount of sand (and not having any gold and lead at all), i.e., Ron is right. Otherwise, print "Hermione".
note: Consider the first sample. Let's start with the 500 grams of sand. Apply the first spell 5 times and turn the sand into 1000 grams of lead. Then apply the second spell 4 times to get 600 grams of gold. Let’s take 400 grams from the resulting amount of gold turn them back into sand. We get 500 grams of sand and 200 grams of gold. If we apply the same operations to 500 grams of sand again, we can get extra 200 grams of gold every time. Thus, you can get 200, 400, 600 etc. grams of gold, i.e., starting with a finite amount of sand (500 grams), you can get the amount of gold which is greater than any preassigned number.
In the forth sample it is impossible to get sand, or lead, or gold, applying the spells.

In the fifth sample an infinitely large amount of gold can be obtained by using only the second spell, which allows you to receive 1 gram of gold out of nothing. Note that if such a second spell is available, then the first and the third one do not affect the answer at all.

The seventh sample is more interesting. We can also start with a zero amount of sand there. With the aid of the third spell you can get sand out of nothing. We get 10000 grams of sand in this manner. Let's get 100 grams of lead using the first spell 100 times. Then make 1 gram of gold from them. We managed to receive 1 gram of gold, starting with a zero amount of sand! Clearly, in this manner you can get an infinitely large amount of gold.

note.ai: 考虑第一个样例。我们从 500 克沙子开始。使用第一个咒语 5 次，将沙子转换为 1000 克铅。然后使用第二个咒语 4 次，得到 600 克黄金。取出其中的 400 克黄金，将它们转换回沙子。此时我们得到 500 克沙子和 200 克黄金。如果再次对 500 克沙子进行相同的操作，每次都可以额外获得 200 克黄金。因此，可以得到 200 克、400 克、600 克等黄金；也就是说，从有限数量的沙子（500 克）出发，可以获得多于任意预先指定数值的黄金。
在第四个样例中，无论施放这些法术，都不可能得到沙子、铅或金子。
在第五个样例中，只使用第二个法术就可以获得无限多的金子，因为该法术允许你凭空得到 1 克金子。注意，如果有这样的第二个法术，那么第一个和第三个法术完全不会影响答案。
第七个样例更加有趣。在那里，我们也可以从 0 克沙子开始。借助第三个法术，你可以凭空得到沙子。这样我们就能得到 10000 克沙子。接着使用第一个法术 100 次，得到 100 克铅。然后用这些铅制成 1 克金子。我们成功地从 0 克沙子开始获得了 1 克金子！显然，用这种方法可以得到无限多的金子。

legend.ai: 很久以前（可能甚至是在第一本书中），伟大的炼金术士、魔法石的创造者尼古拉斯·勒梅教给了哈利·波特三种有用的咒语。第一个咒语可以将 a 克沙子转换为 b 克铅，第二个咒语可以将 c 克铅转换为 d 克黄金，第三个咒语可以将 e 克黄金转换为 f 克沙子。当哈利告诉朋友们这些咒语时，罗恩·韦斯莱惊呆了。毕竟，如果他们能够把沙子变成铅，把铅变成黄金，然后再把一部分黄金变回沙子，如此循环往复，那么就可以从少量沙子开始，获得大量黄金！甚至是无限多的黄金！相比之下，赫敏·格兰杰对这个想法持怀疑态度。她认为，根据物质守恒定律，即使使用魔法，也不可能获得无限多的物质。相反，物质的总量甚至可能在转换过程中减少，因为有一部分物质会转化为魔法能量。尽管赫敏的理论听起来很有说服力，罗恩却不愿相信她。在罗恩看来，赫敏是为了阻止哈利和罗恩把时间浪费在这种无聊的事情上，并让他们去做作业，才编造了物质守恒定律。正因如此，罗恩已经收集了一定数量的沙子，准备进行实验。朋友之间的争吵似乎不可避免了……
请帮助哈利判断他的哪位朋友是正确的，并避免这场争吵。为此，你需要确定：是否可以从一定数量的沙子出发，获得多于任意预先指定数值的黄金。

input.ai: 第一行包含 6 个整数 a、b、c、d、e、f（0 ≤ a，b，c，d，e，f ≤ 1000）。

output.ai: 如果可以仅凭一定数量的有限沙子（且一开始没有任何黄金和铅）获得无限多的黄金，则输出 "Ron"，即罗恩是正确的。否则，输出 "Hermione"。
